name: tomorrow-never-knows
description: FAMOUS DRUM SOUND #2: The Beatles 'Tomorrow Never Knows' (Ringo / Geoff Emerick, Abbey Road 1966). The OPPOSITE axis from the Bonham 'fool-in-the-rain' recipe: heavily COMPRESSED with audible PUMP/breathing (not glue), DARK/lo-fi/saturated (not warm-open), and NARROW/mono (not wide-room), tom-FORWARD. Anchored on the authentic Fairchild 660 (mono tube vari-mu) driven hard, dark Studer 15 IPS tape, dark EQ, and a hard mono-narrow. This is the TONE, not Ringo's tom GROOVE, and it wants TOM mics in the source. Chain-validated 2026-06-03 on the Ship Studios kit (which has NO toms -> a kick+snare-forward fallback balance).
pipeline: 1. SOURCE: phase-aligned multi-mic stems WITH toms (rack/floor) + kick + snare + overheads + room. (No toms -> tom-FORWARD is impossible; fall back to kick+snare-forward and you get the TONE but not the tom dominance.)

2. PER-STEM PROCESS: scripts/mix/process_stems.py with presets/mix/tomorrow-never-knows-stem-process.plans.json (declick OFF; DARK + gentle: HPF, de-box, NO air; damped kick, resonant-but-controlled toms) -> <kit>/processed-tnk/.
3. TOM-FORWARD balance: scripts/mix/balance_stems.py (toms + kick + snare FORWARD; overheads/room controlled; close & dark, NOT roomy) -> bus_tnk_pre.wav.
4. TNK BUS: scripts/mix/tomorrow_never_knows_bus.py bus_tnk_pre.wav bus_tnk.wav (Fairchild pump -> Studer 15 IPS dark tape -> dark EQ -> mono narrow; params in that script).

balance_targets_lufs._method: measured integrated LUFS per stem; one global -6 dBFS-peak headroom trim. TOM-FORWARD + close-mic forward; overheads/room pulled back (TNK is close & dark, the heavy comp brings the ambience UP as the pump).

overhead._note: cymbals back + dark (TNK is not cymbal-forward)

drum room._note: feeds the pump; the Fairchild swells it

balance_targets_lufs._no_toms_fallback: If the kit has no toms (e.g. the Ship Studios / artifacts/drums kits): kick in -16 / snare top -17 / overhead -22 / drum room -22 / kick beater -26 / snare bottom -30 / snare reverb -26. You get the TNK tone (crush/dark/mono) but kick+snare lead instead of toms.

bus_chain._impl: scripts/mix/tomorrow_never_knows_bus.py — authoritative; a bare invocation reproduces these.

2_fairchild_660._intent: the era/Abbey-Road comp, MONO tube vari-mu, driven HARD for the audible PUMP. NOTE: this build COLORS more than it crushes (holds crest), so the pump is GENTLER than the over-limited 1966 original — add the LA-3A stage for more crush. thresh HIGHER = more GR; headroom LOWER = hotter (lore-inverted); sc_filt Off = full-range detection = max pump/dark.

3_la3a_optional._intent: opto LIMIT, HF-emphasis 0 (full-range, darkest, max GR) = genuine crest reduction + odd-harmonic grit. The real TNK crush.

4_studer_a800_tape._intent: dark, fat tape glue (the authentic Studer J37 is Arturia DAW-only/passthrough headless, so this A800 is the headless proxy). repro_hf_eq LOW = darker top.

5_vibe_optional._intent: lo-fi tape grit + band-limit (UADx Vibe Analog Machines / Verve). Pushes darker + adds the saturated 1966 grit.

6_eq_post_zero_phase: high_shelf -4.0 @ 8000 (DARK — remove air, TNK has no top)

7_stereo_narrow._intent: collapse toward MONO (the 1966 image); also monos via the Fairchild (mono unit).

bus_chain.8_output: peak-normalize to -1 dBFS (mix bus — NOT mastered)

approved_signature_full_kit._measured_on: the Fairchild-only DEFAULT on a 60 s active window (240-300 s) of the Ship Studios kit (NO toms -> kick+snare-forward fallback balance). Pre-bus was centroid 2271 / tilt -3.18 / crest 20.9 / corr 0.908.
approved_signature_full_kit._what_to_check: the DIRECTION: centroid DOWN hard (warm/dark, ~-770 here), tilt more negative (dark), crest DOWN (the pump — gentler with Fairchild-only, ~17 with --la3a), correlation UP toward ~0.99 (NARROW/mono — the defining TNK image). Crest/centroid are content-dependent; this section was already dark (tilt -3.18) so it landed very dark (1498). On a brighter/tom kit expect higher.

notes: Needs TOM mics for the tom-FORWARD balance; without them you get the TNK tone (crush/dark/mono) but kick+snare lead.
This is the TONE, not Ringo's hypnotic tom GROOVE — that lives in the source performance.

The repo Fairchild COLORS more than it CRUSHES (holds crest), so the Fairchild-only pump is gentler than the 1966 over-limited original. For the heavy crush, use --la3a (opto LIMIT, genuine crest reduction) and/or --vibe (lo-fi grit). The tuning workflow A/Bs them.
DARK is the point: 15 IPS + repro_hf LOW + high-shelf CUT + NO air anywhere. On an already-dark source it can over-darken (centroid ~1500) — ease --repro-hf up and --dark toward -2 if muddy.
MONO/narrow is the defining image: width 0.35 + the mono Fairchild. Do not 'widen' it.

Honest proxy: the authentic Studer J37 (Arturia) is passthrough headless -> Studer A800 stands in; the exact 1966 compressor is debated (Fairchild 660 / Altec) -> Fairchild 660 is the era/Abbey-Road choice here.
MIX bus (peak -1, NOT mastered) -> hand to master-track; loops via loops-to-deliverables.
